issues.note: Sense 1 already covers organizing how something is done; no separate use exists.
Not a distinct use; it is covered by sense 1, make plans.
'arrange to meet' is standard. The learner error concerns object plus infinitive; no contradiction.
The 'put in order' sense never takes a direct -ing complement.
'arranged meeting' is ungrammatical; arrange takes a to-infinitive.
A passive of a transitive verb illustrates the underlying verb + object pattern.
Wrong: 'arrange to do something' (We arranged to meet) is a core pattern.
Correct diagnosis and fix: 'arranged to meet her'.

findings.F1: Sense 1 example 'I've arranged meeting her at noon.' uses -ing where arrange needs a to-infinitive.
findings.F2: Sense 2 grammar lists the pattern 'verb + -ing form', which the put-in-order sense does not take.
